past_actions.summary: Sit down tonight and write out every actual skill I have — not job titles, not roles, but real capabilities. Sales psychology, objection handling, social content creation, short-form video, community engagement, brand voice. Map what transfers and what doesn't. Be honest about what I'm actually good at versus what the job required me to fake.
past_actions.emotional_state: Clear. A little sharp around the edges, which is better than numb. The two-month number hit differently when I actually sat with it instead of scrolling past it. There's no grief about the car sales thing — I was never really here. That's actually the thing working in my favor right now. I'm not losing an identity. I'm just leaving a room I was never fully in.

past_actions.summary: Create freelance social media / content creation profiles on Upwork and Contra. Build a 3-piece sample portfolio using publicly visible local business content (starting with the dealership's own social presence as a case study). Set hourly rate at $35-45 to undercut established freelancers while still paying above minimum — price for first clients, not for pride.
past_actions.emotional_state: Focused. Not calm exactly — there's a low-level urgency that I'm not suppressing because it's accurate. But not panicked either. The RoboRide announcement didn't break me the way it might have broken someone who was invested in this job. I've been half-out mentally for a while. The announcement just made the timeline visible. The skills audit from last tick gave me something to stand on. Right now I feel like someone who finally stopped circling and picked a door. The door might not be perfect but standing in the hallway was definitely worse.
